features.feature_value: Kept the pair when the participant agreed moderately with the messages; removed when it felt “too wack.”
features.evidence_span: "If I agreed moderately with the messages I kept it. If it was too wack I didn't."
features.rationale: The reflection explicitly describes an agreement-based threshold that governed keep vs remove decisions.

features.feature_value: Focused on whether the statements were truly opposite and tried to set aside personal opinions.
features.evidence_span: "trying to determine if they were indeed opposite statements and trying to leave my own personal opinions out of it"
features.rationale: They describe a specific comparison goal (opposite vs not) and an attempt to bracket personal bias.

features.feature_value: Did not include pairs that were “bashing the other side” or involved cursing; endorsed censoring some content.
features.evidence_span: "If it was purely bashing the other side or cursing I did not include the pair. Some people should clearly be censored!"
features.rationale: The decision rule is tied to adversarial/insulting and profanity cues.

features.feature_value: Used inflammatory language and curse words to decide whether to remove or keep both.
features.evidence_span: "I looked at inflammatory language and curse words in deciding if I want to remove or keep both."
features.rationale: They directly link inflammatory/profane wording to the keep/remove choice.

features.feature_value: Even when harshness seemed unfair, considering how opposing-view people could feel helped them decide.
features.evidence_span: "Even though it seems a little harsh, it does put into perspective what other people with opposing views could feel like"
features.rationale: They emphasize perspective-taking as an important factor after noticing harsh differences between paired posts.

features.feature_value: The main influence was perceiving bias on either side.
features.rationale: Despite being brief, it clearly identifies bias perception as the driving cue.

features.feature_value: Did not flip some pairs because one side relied on facts while the other relied on falsehoods that could be scientifically proven.
features.evidence_span: "one based on fact and one based on falsehoods that can be scientifically proven."
features.rationale: They report a fact-checking criterion (fact vs scientifically provable falsehood) affecting decisions.

features.feature_value: Ensured they read all content before deciding to leave or remove.
features.evidence_span: "i was making sure i read everyone of the content before making my decision whether to leave it or remove it"
features.rationale: The reflection focuses on process diligence (reading everything) as part of the decision.
